subject: Cosmos Energy — cluster landing inventory, NVMe vs SAN decisions and contract items
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Kunal Mehta <kunal@cosmospower.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Oct 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cosmos Energy — cluster landing inventory, NVMe vs SAN decisions and contract items

Hi Kunal / Priya —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our intake, we need a short, validated inventory and a decision on local NVMe vs SAN for two things: the KV cache (low-latency hotspot state) and the model artifact store (large, read-heavy). We want to lock these decisions before DocuSign so the Reserved Capacity and on-site acceptance criteria match reality.

Key asks from our side (can you confirm by EOD Tue?):
- Rack IDs / cross-connect type and port count for the deployment rack(s).
- Whether local NVMe is allowed on inference nodes (warranty / vendor policy). If disallowed, confirm SAN performance profile (IOPS/latency / host-facing protocol: iSCSI/Fibre/SMB).
- Expected sustained egress limits and any egress filtering that will block outbound telemetry to our control plane.
- KMS integration constraints — can customer KMS/HSM accept Redwood service principal for key wrap, or do we use vault-to-vault?

Our proposal (attached sheet):
- KV cache: local NVMe (ephemeral) on worker nodes for lowest tail latency; 3x replicas across AZ-equivalent racks with periodic snapshotting to persistent store.
- Model artifacts: network-backed storage (SAN or S3-compatible on-prem) with a model-cache layer on node local SSDs for hot models.
- CSI drivers: prefer vendor-supported iSCSI/FC driver or Rook-Ceph (if customer wants software-defined).

Attachments: cosmos_inventory_v1.xlsx (please fill in missing rack / switch serials), provision_template_v3.yaml (example nodepools + storage classes).

If local NVMe is a showstopper, we’ll outline an alternative architecture that shifts caching to a dedicated NVMe appliance or larger memory-only cache (higher cost).

Thanks —
Camila
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai

From: Kunal Mehta <kunal@cosmospower.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@cosmospower.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Oct 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cosmos Energy — cluster landing inventory, NVMe vs SAN decisions and contract items

Camila —

Quick answers after chatting with infra ops here: we can provide the inventory but a few constraints to note:

1) Local NVMe: our hardware warranty and the on-site vendor (RackLink) do allow NVMe on compute nodes, but only if SSD firmware is vendor-managed and part of the BOM. We cannot allow customer-managed raw NVMe modules. Practically: we can provision worker nodes with vendor-provisioned NVMe; scope needs to be explicit in BOM.

2) SAN: we have a NetApp FAS cluster exposed over iSCSI to the private VLAN. Baseline performance: 20k sustained IOPS per host aggregate, typical read latency 6-8ms. If you need sub-ms tail latency for KV, that will require local NVMe.

3) Egress: outbound to redwood-control.redwood.ai on 443 is allowed but must terminate at a proxy IP — we’ll provide allowed IPs. No other outbound ports.

4) KMS: we have a Thales Luna appliance. Integrations require provisioning a client cert; we can do that but it needs to be coordinated through our security/PKI team and will add ~2 weeks to the on-site schedule.

Attached is a filled inventory excerpt (I added rack IDs and switch models). Happy to review the provision template.

Kunal
Head of Infrastructure, Cosmos Energy
kunal@cosmospower.com

Attachment: cosmos_inventory_v1.xlsx (excerpt provided)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Kunal Mehta <kunal@cosmospower.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Oct 2029 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cosmos Energy — cluster landing inventory, NVMe vs SAN decisions and contract items

Thanks Kunal — helpful details. Based on NetApp iSCSI numbers, here's a pragmatic nodepool + storage proposal (high-level):

Nodepools:
- control-plane: 3x m6a-24 (or on-prem equivalent) — small PVCs for etcd (RAID1 across SAN), dedicated management NIC.
- inference-gpu-hot: 8x GPU nodes (A100-equivalent) with vendor-managed local NVMe (1.6TB) for model cache + KV hotset (ephemeral).
- inference-gpu-cold: 6x GPU nodes without local NVMe; model artifacts read from SAN (warm cache on 120GB local NVMe).
- stateful-backups: 2x nodes with direct SAN attachment for backups and snapshot storage.

Storage classes:
- local-ephemeral-nvme (fastest, no snapshots): used for KV cache with application-level snapshot to persistent store every 5 minutes.
- block-san (iSCSI, replicated): primary persistent store for model artifacts and etcd backups.
- object-onprem (S3-compatible gateway): bulk artifact repository for cold models.

Acceptance criteria (to include in SOW):
- KV P99 tail latency < 6ms for cached keys during 95% load profile (measured in pre-acceptance soak).
- Model pull concurrency: N=25 concurrent pulls of 4GB model under 2.5s median fetch time from local cache; from SAN under 350ms per 100MB (depends on SAN cache).
- KMS: successful wrap/unwrap test using provided client cert with Thales in test rack.

Open question for Cosmos: are you comfortable with vendor-managed NVMe (we will treat devices as ephemeral for maintenance)? If so, we’ll move forward with the hot nodepool profile and adjust the SOW. If not, we will design a deployment with dedicated NVMe appliance (higher ops cost).

I attached a lightweight provision_template_v3.yaml with node selectors and storage class hints.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Cosmos Energy — cluster landing inventory, NVMe vs SAN decisions and contract items

Kunal / team —

A couple of network items to lock now to avoid rework during on-site provisioning:

1) Cross-connects / VLANs: we need two dedicated VLANs per rack: "redwood-control" (management, restricted egress) and "redwood-data" (worker/data plane). Please confirm VLAN IDs and allowed MTU (we prefer 9000 for jumbo frames on the data VLAN).

2) BGP / routing: if you have L3 aggregation in the rack, we’ll peer via BGP for the external NAT addresses used by the cluster egress gateway. If you prefer L2 cross-connect, specify. Provide expected route propagation time windows during cutover.

3) Firewall / proxy: provide the proxy IP(s) that terminate 443 for redwood-control.redwood.ai so our outbound health checks and tracing endpoints can reach the control plane. Also confirm whether TLS inspection is enabled — if so, we need cert pinning options.

4) Maintenance window: propose Saturdays 0200-0600 local time for node reboots, firmware updates, and disk replacement. Any blackout dates?

If Kunal confirms vendor-managed NVMe is acceptable, we’ll plan for driver install steps (vendor agent + CSI) during the first-day runbook and include an automated device-claim playbook so we can label volumes ephemeral for eviction.

Neha
Network PM, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai

1) Kunal / Priya: confirm vendor-managed NVMe on the BOM (yes/no) and share the final BOM line items by Wed EOD. Attach: cosmos_inventory_v1.xlsx (we'll reconcile).
2) Kunal: provide proxy egress IPs and confirm TLS inspection status.
3) Kunal: coordinate security/PKI contact for Thales client cert; target 2-week lead.
4) Neha: after VLAN IDs and MTU are provided, we'll produce a short runbook (day 0 - day 3) including CSI driver steps and BGP peer snippets.
5) Karthik: draft SOW acceptance criteria snippet for our procurement/finance team (will include KV P99 and model fetch numbers).

I will attach the updated provision_template_v3.yaml to the DocuSign envelope this afternoon and route the SOW/appendix for signature. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/CE-DEAL-114

If anyone needs to escalate, loop Laura for timelines / commercial questions.

Camila
